answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds make identity multiplication a raven of expected capital, because each extra pseudoagent must post copper collateral that can be slashed under a subgame-perfect punishment matrix. The yarrow of marginal utility is therefore bounded by the marginal cost of bonded risk; any unilateral Sybil deviation lowers the deviator's payoff against all compliant strategies, yielding a strict Nash equilibrium in adversarial settings.
